+### Approval Lifetime On Run And Resume
+
+Use the engine's [run-scoped approval contract](../../../etas-core/docs/architect/etas-residual-checks-design.md#33-run-scoped-approval-and-explicit-reuse).
+The default is memory-only approval for one root run. Completion/failure/cancel
+expires it; same-process and cross-process checkpoint resume use current
+authority and do not inherit old grants or monitor Approved readiness. A retained
+audit/trace file, accepted program boolean or completed approval ledger entry
+is not current authorization.
+
+Run/resume must work without an approval database when the execution can safely
+proceed under this rule. Do not auto-create approval tables/signing keys or
+interpret checkpoint storage/configuration as an approval-reuse opt-in. Only
+explicit application/runtime-profile configuration with a trusted verifying
+provider may enable persistent reuse; checkpoint data cannot choose a provider
+or endpoint. Keep such service composition separate from monitor execution.
 
+An explicit application/source/handler reapproval protocol can use the existing
+stdin broker/UI at a safe continuation. Do not automatically prompt just because
+old approval expired, rewind source or repeat confirmed I/O. Render precise
+engine rejection when no safe authorized continuation exists; absence of an
+optional persistence service is not itself a default-run readiness error.
+
+### Compiler Service Composition For Reflected Code
+
+Reflection/checked generation follows
+[frontend architecture](../../../etas-frontend/docs/architect/etas-reflection-design.md).
+The CLI composes the selected engine's CandidatePublisher with
+etas_driver::compiler's frontend adapter and etas_host::compiler protocol.
+
+Run/resume use the same service setup. Compiler configuration resolves through
+the existing etas.toml/runtime configuration path; do not add a collection of
+undocumented environment variables or a separate eval subprocess command.
+Use the same compiler service for AgentDef<A> and ordinary-flow CallableDef<F>;
+the frontend's checked overload/frozen contract determines A/F. CLI does not
+guess a target from display names or wrap a flow as an agent.
+
+CLI parses options, constructs services and renders structured diagnostics.
+It must not parse/check generated bodies, own the definition registry or
+implement revision/type relocation. Driver remains independent of interpreter;
+the chosen engine supplies its publisher port.
+
+Compiler service availability is distinct from authority to perform Code actions,
+and from authority to execute the resulting candidate. No implicit network/
+filesystem grants or automatic global agent/flow promotion follow from configuration.
+
+No new reflection, publish, replace or run-code command is required by SPEC.
+Evaluation/scoring/selection remain EDK/application work. SPEC has no public
+binary std.compiler.load/export API: public restoration reads saved source and
+locked environment using normal authority, validates the statically typed target
+and compiles again. A binary package/cache artifact is not a CLI execution permit.
+
+Render structured rejected/accepted/guarded reports and CompileError
+rejected/service distinctions. Preserve cancellation, authority denial and
+BudgetExceeded as distinct execution outcomes. Compiler configuration controls
+CPU/memory ceilings with explicit units; queue wait counts toward active WallTime
+and retries/revisions do not create fresh parent budgets.
+
+Residual support follows the
+[shared monitor protocol](../../../etas-core/docs/architect/etas-residual-checks-design.md).
+Compose neutral backend/guard capabilities from the selected engine/services;
+frontend validates them and the engine installs the plans. CLI only renders
+descriptive runtime_checks/guarded reports and structured runtime violations.
+It must not parse check strings, own live monitor state or use an unsafe Host
+TraceSpecRuntimeClient selection as installation proof. run/resume share the
+engine's semantic event and restore gates; disabling trace/profile output cannot
+disable enforcement.
